newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-IAAF HALVE DRUG BANS TO TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF HALVE DRUG BANS TO TWO YEARS.

text.p: The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) halved its ban for serious doping offences from four to two years on Thursday.
On the second and final day of its two-day congress, the IAAF accepted a proposal from several European countries to cut suspensions in an effort to avoid costly civil litigation.
The present four-year ban for first offenders was introduced in 1991 when the sport was still recovering from the 1988 Ben Johnson scandal.
Johnson tested positive for steroids after winning the Seoul Olympic 100 metres final.
The IAAF has come under increasing pressure to cut the ban as civil courts have ruled that it constitutes a restraint of trade.
Two years ago in Gothenburg, the congress rejected a similar resolution after a heated debate when delegates argued a reduction would send the wrong signal to drugs cheats.
